To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal excess of loss retention and limiting levels are obtained as a result of a joint optimization of a risk measure (probability of joint survival up to a finite time horizon) and of a performance measure (expected profits at time x given joint survival).

the probability of joint insurer and reinsurer survival up to a given time x, considered as a risk, is a suitable risk measure for this problem, the expected profits of the insurer and reinsurer at time x, conditional on their joint survival up until that time, is a suitable performance measure for this problem and the efficient frontier approach is suitable for the solution of this problem.

the efficient frontier approach to setting the reinsurance retention and the limit level is a powerful tool for the analysis of the joint survival of the reinsurer and the direct insurer and for the optimal design of reinsurance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of optimal excess-of-loss reinsurance, where the risk is modelled by a non-negative, nondecreasing premium income, a Poisson process for claim arrivals and any continuous joint distribution for claim amounts.

a generalization of the classical problem of excess of loss re-insurance with a single retention level, to the case of a limiting and a single retention level and with the derivation of a solution to a problem of joint optimal survival reinsurance, based on a risk measure and a performance measure, both of them defined on the joint survival probability of the insurer and the reinsured.

a general model for the optimal excess of loss type reinsurance with a retention level and a limiting level, where the premium income and claim severities are modelled by general non-negative, nondecreasing and continuous functions, respectively.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of dependent claim severities, the optimal reinsurance strategy depends on the correlation structure between claim severities.

the efficient frontier approach, based on the expected profit and the probability of joint insurer-reinsurer survival as the performance and the risk measure, respectively, provides a very flexible and powerful tool for the analysis and solution of the optimal joint survival problem of a reinsurance contract with a retention and a limiting level.

the efficient frontier approach, based on the expected profits and the probability of joint ruin as a performance and a risk measure, respectively, is a powerful tool for the determination of the optimal excess of loss limits and retention levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the context of the considered reinsurance model, the efficient frontier approach is applicable for any non-decreasing, non-negative function for the premium income, any continuous joint distribution for the claim severities and, in the context, of the considered optimality problems, for any dependence structure for the claim severeties.

the optimal joint survival reinsurance can be obtained by a joint consideration of the probability of joint insurer's survival as a risk measure, and of the expected profits given joint survival as a performance measure.
the optimal reinsurance problem can be solved by combining the risk measure and the performance measure in an appropriate manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the efficient frontier approach to the optimal excess of loss problem can be applied to a wide class of claim amount models, and that it is very sensitive to the dependence structure between the claims.

, in the presence of a joint survival risk measure, the expected profits at the finite time horizon can be employed to define a joint survival optimal reinsurance treaty, which is Pareto efficient in terms of the joint survival risk measure and the expected profit performance measure.

the optimal retention level is always lower than the optimal limiting level, for any risk aversion parameter and any performance measure, while the optimal retention level decreases with the increase of the risk aversion parameter.
